column1: Report title: Probation and Parole in the United States, 2019 NCJ 256092
Data source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Annual Probation Survey, 2019; and U.S. Census Bureau, National Intercensal Estimates, 2020
Authors: Barbara Oudekerk, Ph.D., former BJS Statistician, and Danielle Kaeble, BJS Statistician

column12: Number on probation per 100,000 adult U.S. residents, December 31, 2019/a

column1: Note: Data quality may vary across jurisdictions for counts of entries and exits. Therefore, the population on December 31, 2019 does not equal the population on January 1, 2019, plus entries, minus exits. Counts may not be actual as reporting agencies may provide estimates on some or all detailed data. Rates are based on the probation population counts as of December 31 of the reporting year and were calculated using U.S. Census Bureau estimates of the U.S. resident population of persons age 18 or older for January 1 of the following year.
a/Reported data will equal estimated data in cases where no imputation was required.
b/Rates were calculated using the estimated U.S. adult resident population in each jurisdiction on January 1, 2020.
c/See Probation: Explanatory notes for 2019 for more details.
Source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Annual Probation Survey, 2019; and U.S. Census Bureau, National Intercensal Estimates, 2020.
